title: When Thou Shalt Come, O Lord
description: When Thou Shalt Come, O Lord in Tonic Solfa to BOYLSTON, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns of the Greek Church (Edinburgh and London, 1900).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Short Metre (6.6.8.6), and this page sets them to BOYLSTON; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: When Thou shalt come, O Lord, Wrapt in Thy glo-ry bright, Then shall the earth in ter-ror quake, The sun with-hold his light.

lines: When Thou shalt come, O Lord,
Wrapt in Thy glory bright,
Then shall the earth in terror quake,
The sun withhold his light.
When Thou shalt come, O Lord,
Then to Thy judgment-bar,
Even as a mighty stream, shall flow
The sons of men from far.
When Thou shalt come, O Lord,
Then shall the books be spread,
And from their secrets Thou shalt judge
The living and the dead.
When Thou shalt come, O Lord,
Then save me by Thy power,
Let not the flames of wrath o'ertake
Thy servant in that hour.
When Thou shalt come, O Lord,
In mercy let me stand —
No guilt upon my conscience laid —
Approved, at Thy right hand.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns of the Greek Church (1900)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns of the Greek Church; set to BOYLSTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
